# RETRO t4-12415

## What worked
- Neutral shared brief plus targeted cross-examination: Sol's source-only toggle finding was narrowed by Opus tracing Hyprland/Quickshell input routing; Opus's docs finding was independently confirmed by Sol.
- Opus mutant-based fixture (32 gated cases, sealed) made test-validity claims concrete.

## Process deviations
- Harness refused the omarchy-reviewer subagent's Write of opus/report.md ("Subagents should return findings as text"). Coordinator did not write it on the subagent's behalf; the final report and follow-up answer exist as returned messages in the native subagent transcript. The subagent agent definition / brief output rule conflicts with the harness: the workflow should either let the coordinator record returned reports as coordinator-authored copies (explicit user decision) or change the agent definition.
- Opus self-reported: one host `python3 -c "pass"` run outside review.py, two reads over 50 lines (59, 51), one `cut -c` output not relied on (opus/RETRO.md).
- Sol finished its initial pass in 4.9 minutes (source-only, 21-line report); coverage was adequate for this small PR.
- Startup memory context of the coordinator/subagent was not separately verified with a no-memory control; no prior-PR technical content was observed.

## Carry forward
- Resolve the subagent report-file rule before the next assignment.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** `omarchy setup welcome` works as described. No runtime defect was found in the tested scope. The notes below cover two ineffective test assertions, untested first-run wiring and stale documentation.

- The dispatcher resolves `omarchy setup welcome [--all]`, lists it under `omarchy setup` and `omarchy commands`, and `omarchy commands --check` passes.
- Without `--all`, the command sends the same "Learn Keybindings" notification as the previous `welcome.sh`: identical arguments, glyph, real newline and `--exec omarchy-menu-keybindings` target.
- `--all` adds the "Getting Started" notification with `--exec omarchy-menu`. Unknown options exit 1 without sending anything.
- `install/user/first-run/welcome.sh` now sends both notifications. A failed send still makes the step exit nonzero, so first-run retries it as before.

### Two assertions in `setup-welcome-test.sh` cannot fail

| Line | Assertion | Why it never catches a regression |
|---|---|---|
| 39 | `! grep -Fq -- '--exec omarchy-menu$'` | `-F` makes `$` a literal character, so the pattern never matches. A `!` pipeline also does not trigger `set -e`. |
| 46 | `grep -Fq -- '--exec omarchy-menu'` | This also matches `--exec omarchy-menu-keybindings`, which is always present in the `--all` log. |

**Optional test improvement:** with the current test, a `--all` notification whose click target was changed to another command, or duplicated as `omarchy-menu-keybindings`, still passed. With the change below, both of those variants failed, and so did a default run that sends both notifications. The unmodified command still passed.

```diff
-! grep -Fq -- '--exec omarchy-menu$' "$TEST_LOG"
+if grep -q -- '--exec omarchy-menu$' "$TEST_LOG"; then
+  echo "default run sent the menu notification" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
 ...
-grep -Fq -- '--exec omarchy-menu' "$TEST_LOG"
+grep -q -- '--exec omarchy-menu$' "$TEST_LOG"
```

**Optional test improvement:** no test runs the changed first-run step. The new test calls a copy of `bin/omarchy-setup-welcome` directly. `test/shell.d/first-run-test.sh` stubs first-run as already complete, so it exits at the completion gate before any step runs. That test still passed with `welcome.sh` replaced by `exit 1`. A small case could run `install/user/first-run/welcome.sh` with a stub `omarchy-notification-send` first on `PATH` and expect two sends. That would catch a renamed command or a dropped `--all`.

**Documentation:** `docs/file-layout.md` (lines 288-291 at this head) still describes `welcome.sh` as a single keybindings toast. The removed comment explaining real newlines and the three-line card limit applies to the body that now lives in `bin/omarchy-setup-welcome`. Moving it there would keep that guidance next to the text it protects.

**Optional:** the new notification uses `--exec omarchy-menu`, which defaults to `toggle`. From source, a pointer click cannot reach the toast while the menu is open. However, invoking the newest notification with Super + Alt + comma while the menu is open closes the menu instead of showing it. `--exec omarchy-menu summon` (as `setup-agent.hook` already does) would always show the root menu. One trade-off: unlike `toggle`, `summon` replaces an active scripted picker without signalling its caller. This was traced in source only, not tested in a running session.

---

**Test scope:** pinned head `58aa72c`. The command, the first-run `welcome.sh` step, the PR test with mutated copies of the command, `omarchy commands --check` and `first-run-test.sh` were run in an isolated sandbox with a stub notification sender. Notification and menu click behavior was assessed from source, including Hyprland 0.56.2 and Quickshell 0.3.1 source for input routing (installed versions not confirmed). The full `test/cli` and `test/shell` suites were not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up questions, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
